original_poem:
అనుమంత వంశం దారి తీస్తున్నది, 
అంతులేని శక్తి, పితామహుల నుండి. 
సముద్రాన్ని చీల్చి వెళ్ళిన
వీరుల వేర్లు ఈ నేలలో గాఢం,
అదిగో వాటి చిహ్నాలు.
translated_poem:
The ancestral line leads the way, 
Unfathomable strength, passed down from forefathers. 
Roots of heroes who crossed the ocean, 
Deeply embedded in this soil, 
There lie their marks.

stanzas.loss_note: సముద్రాన్ని చీల్చి వెళ్ళిన (those who split/crossed the ocean) carries a specific mythological resonance in Telugu cultural memory — possibly evoking the Ramayana crossing of the sea — rendered as generic 'crossed the ocean', the heroic-mythological weight is softened.

cultural_entities.translation_note: Vamsam (lineage/clan) is a culturally specific Telugu-Sanskrit term for ancestral lineage with ritual and social significance; rendered as 'ancestral line', the clan-identity weight is partially lost.
Pitamahulu (forefathers/patriarchal ancestors) carries a Sanskrit-rooted reverential register in Telugu culture; 'forefathers' approximates but loses the patrilineal-sacred connotation.
